title: Gold Session Behavior: How XAUUSD Acts in Asia, London and New York
seoTitle: Gold Session Behavior: Asia, London & New York XAUUSD Guide | TradePilot
seoDescription: XAUUSD behaves differently in each session: Asia builds ranges, London sweeps them, New York delivers trends and reversals. Learn the session map ICT traders use on gold.
excerpt: Gold is not a 24-hour market in character — it is three markets stitched together. Here is how XAUUSD typically behaves through the Asian, London and New York sessions, and why it matters.
author: TradePilot Research

content.text: Ask two traders what gold "does" and you may get opposite answers, because they are probably trading different sessions. XAUUSD is not one uniform market — it is three overlapping markets with different participants, different liquidity profiles and different personalities. Learning the session map is one of the highest-leverage upgrades an intraday gold trader can make.

The Asian session is the quietest period for gold, dominated by regional flows and thinner institutional participation. Price typically **consolidates in a narrow range**, often centered around a level of balance from the prior New York afternoon. For the ICT-minded trader, Asia's job is construction: its high and low become the first meaningful [liquidity pools](/blog/what-is-a-liquidity-sweep) that later sessions will test. Breakouts during Asian hours are notoriously unreliable precisely because the liquidity to sustain them is absent — most Asian "breakouts" simply deliver price to the other side of the range before mean-reverting.

The London open is where gold's personality changes. European bank flow arrives, spreads tighten, and the session frequently opens with a **raid on the Asian range**: a sweep of the Asian low followed by reversal (or the high, in bearish days) as stops resting beyond the range are absorbed. This London sweep-and-reverse is among the most studied ICT patterns on gold, and it explains why so many Asian-range breakout traders get chopped. The strongest moves of the day often start here — but so do the sharpest fakeouts.

content.title: Kill Zones
content.text: ICT calls these windows Kill Zones: the London Open Kill Zone (~02:00–05:00 ET) and the New York Open Kill Zone (~07:00–10:00 ET). They are not magic hours — they are simply the periods when institutional order flow makes setups worth taking actually resolve, instead of drifting.

New York brings U.S. data — CPI, NFP, FOMC, ISM — and with it the day's largest volume. Two typical constructions exist. In a **Judas swing day**, price runs the London direction first, sweeps an early New York level, then reverses into the true daily trend. In a **continuation day**, the London move retraces briefly into a [fair value gap](/blog/what-is-a-fair-value-gap) or [order block](/blog/what-is-an-order-block) and resumes. After roughly 11:00 ET, gold's intraday edge decays quickly: lunchtime liquidity thins, ranges compress, and setups that would have resolved cleanly at 9:30 instead chop. Most intraday ICT traders on gold simply stop trading the afternoon.

items: **Pre-Asia:** mark the previous day's high/low, weekly open and any daily-level [premium/discount](/blog/premium-and-discount-explained) boundaries.
**End of Asia:** record the Asian high and low — these are the day's first pools. Note where price sits inside the prior day's range.
**London open:** watch how the range breaks. A sweep that fails to find acceptance beyond the Asian extreme is a signal to prepare for the reversal model — not to chase the breakout.

**New York open:** evaluate whether London's move was Judas or genuine, check [XAU/XAG SMT divergence](/blog/smt-divergence-between-gold-and-silver) at the key levels, and trade only what the model defines.
**After 11:00 ET:** journal, review, and let the market build tomorrow's ranges.

content.text: News is a session property, not an afterthought

Because U.S. data releases land inside the New York Kill Zone, session awareness and news awareness are the same discipline. Gold's reaction to CPI is not a tradable "setup" in itself — spreads blow out, slippage spikes and levels stop meaning anything for the first seconds. The practical rule most systematic traders adopt: no entries in the minutes immediately around releases; let the initial volatility sweep a level and *then* trade the model's response to it.

Session context is built into the engine: pools, sweeps and signals are all timestamped against the Asian/London/New York map, and the quality score reflects whether a setup formed inside a Kill Zone.
